title: Gas Station
summary: Given n gas stations along a circular route, where the amount of gas at the i-th station is gas[i] and the cost to travel from the i-th station to the (i+1)-th station is cost[i], determine the starting gas station's index from which you can complete a full circuit.
statement: Given n gas stations along a circular route, where the amount of gas at the i-th station is gas[i] and the cost to travel from the i-th station to the (i+1)-th station is cost[i], determine the starting gas station's index from which you can complete a full circuit. If no such starting station exists, return -1. If a solution exists, it is guaranteed to be unique.
constraints: Arrays have equal length from 1 to 100000; every gas/cost value is between 0 and 10000.
Start with an empty unlimited tank, collect gas at each station, then pay its outgoing cost. Complete a full clockwise circuit without a negative tank.
Return the unique valid zero-based start if one exists; otherwise return -1. Inputs never have multiple valid starts.
hints: Total fuel determines whether any complete circuit is possible, but not which station works.
Scan once with a candidate start and its running tank; a negative tank invalidates every start in that attempted segment.
After a failure set start=index+1 and tank=0; keep a separate total balance across all stations. Return -1 if the total is negative.
Zero tank is allowed. A failure occurs only below zero, and the uniqueness guarantee removes any tie rule.
editorial: If the tank from a candidate first becomes negative at station i, every later start inside that attempted segment also fails by i: it loses a nonnegative prefix balance. Skip the whole segment and try i+1. Track the global total separately; a negative total makes every circuit impossible. Otherwise the surviving candidate completes the circle. The independent oracle simulates all possible starts and explicitly rejects generated inputs violating the unique-answer guarantee.

tests.explanation: Starting at index 3 leaves balances 3,6,4,2,0 after successive legs, completing the circle.
Total fuel is 9 while total cost is 10, so every starting choice fails.
